This one has always stuck with me. Whenever you are going to get up and leave a room, pick 3 small things you can do before you go. The great thing about this is that it helps you commute items around your house - something you would otherwise not do because you don't want to get up / leave the room! But in this case, you're leaving the room anyway, so before you go, you may look around the room and realize, "Hmm. Those chips should go back in the kitchen. And I can put those books back on my desk. And let me hang up this one shirt." And you're done!

The 3 "things" you choose can be an actual thing (like the bag of chips), a related group of things (like the books), or an activity (like hanging up a shirt - which could easily become hanging up 2-3 shirts, or more, but remember not to get carried away). Again, by picking to do these when you are leaving the room, i.e., already in action, you are working off of the natural momentum of your life, and not forcing yourself to break an activity or set aside a specific chunk of time in order to clean.

I like to do this at least once a day, but I usually do it more often, or do more things (5 things, or 5 minutes worth of things, etc., or until I want to stop). You find that it is nice to do this, as it serves to gently rebalance your space. Try for a few times a week to really see a difference. Also, you'll see that the more you do it, the easier it gets, because you will usually be doing the same type of activities. Now, reflecting on what these activities are, and examining them at the source to see how to prevent needing a clean-up in the first place, that's a tip for another day...!
